metadata.title: North Carolina data center moratoria
metadata.note: Records what local governments have decided about new data centers; it says nothing about where data centers exist or are planned. Estimated expiration dates are labelled '(estimated)'. Records outlined in black need confirmation against a primary source. Records changed by research after the base table carry 'updated' and 'update_note'.
metadata.boundaries: U.S. Census Bureau, 2021 cartographic boundary files

properties.name: Beaufort County
properties.covers: acceptance, processing and approval of all new data center applications (proposed)
properties.update_note: Vote on a proposed one-year moratorium postponed to 2026-10-05.

properties.name: Camden County
properties.covers: data centers; cryptocurrency mining; data processing

properties.name: Chatham County
properties.covers: data centers; data processing facilities; cryptocurrency mining

properties.name: Clay County
properties.covers: commercial data centers with a peak power demand of 2 megawatts or more, in unincorporated Clay County
properties.update_note: Adoption date and permanence now documented: 5-0 on 2026-01-08, a permanent ban on 2 MW and larger.

properties.name: Durham County
properties.covers: new or expanded data centers; exempt only if UNDER 100,000 sq ft AND closed-loop cooling AND no diesel backup generators

properties.name: Forsyth County
properties.update_note: Straw vote 4-3 on 2026-09-14 to have staff prepare a possible six-month moratorium for 2026-09-28.

properties.name: Guilford County
properties.covers: new data center projects in unincorporated Guilford County
properties.update_note: Voted 2026-09-17 to schedule an Oct. 15 hearing on a moratorium of up to 180 days.

properties.name: Halifax County
properties.update_note: Voted 5-1 to schedule an Oct. 19 hearing on a possible moratorium.

properties.name: Jackson County
properties.covers: data center development permits (zoning, development, building, demolition), related site plans, and rezoning for data center use

properties.name: Macon County
properties.covers: data centers (8am-5pm operating hours, no cargo-container/trailer operation, 750-foot setback)

properties.name: McDowell County
properties.update_note: Adopted a six-month moratorium 2026-08-31, two days after the snapshot.

properties.name: Nash County
properties.covers: data centers, data processing facilities and cryptocurrency mining in unincorporated areas
properties.duration: until 2027-06-30 or until new UDO rules are adopted
properties.update_note: Adopted a moratorium 2026-09-08 for unincorporated areas, through 2027-06-30.

properties.name: Northampton County
properties.expiration_note: Adoption, the 32-month term and the unanimous vote are confirmed. The end date is not: the term was changed on the floor.

properties.name: Pasquotank County
properties.update_note: Still in effect; a draft UDO that would ban data centers outright went public 2026-09-14.

properties.name: Randolph County
properties.covers: data centers (conditional zoning, impact/sound studies, closed-loop cooling, generator limits, decommissioning bonds)

properties.name: Warren County
properties.covers: development approvals for data centers and related high-impact facilities (special/conditional use permits, rezonings, building permits)

properties.name: Watauga County
properties.covers: data centers, crypto mining facilities and similar uses
properties.update_note: County minutes now retrieved: adopted 5-0 on 2026-04-21 for one year.

properties.name: Perquimans County
properties.covers: special use permits and other development approvals for data centers and cryptocurrency mining (proposed)
properties.update_note: The 2026-09-08 hearing went ahead on a one-year draft, but the outcome has not been published.
properties.confirmation_note: The advertised public hearing on 2026-09-08 appears to have gone ahead, but the county has posted no minutes and no outlet covered it, so whether the moratorium was adopted is unknown.

properties.name: City of Charlotte
properties.covers: data centers (projects already in the development pipeline exempt)
properties.update_note: A nine-month extension is still pending: it never reached the council's 2026-09-14 agenda.
properties.expiration_note: A nine-month extension has been proposed but not voted: no data center item appears on the council's published agendas through 2026-09-21. If it passes before 2026-11-05, this end date moves.

properties.name: City of Greensboro
properties.covers: data centers / data storage & processing facilities with electrical demand over 10 MW

properties.name: City of Kings Mountain
properties.duration: 182 days, extended by one year on 2026-08-25
properties.update_note: Extension confirmed: one year from 2026-08-25.

properties.name: City of Lincolnton
properties.update_note: Re-checked: no report of the September vote the council promised.

properties.name: City of Mount Airy
properties.covers: new or expanded data centers and cryptocurrency mining in zoned areas
properties.duration: 60 days, extended by 90 days on 2026-09-03 (150 days total)
properties.update_note: Extended by 90 days on 2026-09-03, so it did not lapse in September.

properties.name: City of Raleigh
properties.update_note: Council directed a six-month moratorium to be drafted 2026-09-15; vote set for 2026-10-06.

properties.name: City of Salisbury
properties.covers: data centers (size, noise and water restrictions)

properties.name: City of Southport
properties.covers: new data center approvals while the city writes zoning standards
properties.update_note: Adopted unanimously 2026-09-10 after the public hearing; 15 months.

properties.name: City of Statesville
properties.covers: acceptance, processing and approval of development applications for data centers
properties.update_note: Second reading passed 2026-09-14; the 180-day moratorium is now in effect.

properties.name: City of Whiteville
properties.update_note: Adopted a 12-month moratorium 2026-08-25, four days before the snapshot.

properties.name: City of Wilson
properties.covers: data centers; cryptocurrency mining; battery storage

properties.name: Town of Bailey
properties.covers: data centers (a definition critics called broad enough to reach ordinary business computer networks)
properties.update_note: Confirmed by the Spring Hope Enterprise: 3-1 vote on 2026-05-18 for 10 months.

properties.name: Town of Black Mountain
properties.covers: data centers limited to heavy industrial zones, quarter-mile setback from residences/schools/places of worship, 50 dB nighttime cap at property line

properties.name: Town of Cary
properties.covers: data centers over 1 MW — development approvals, rezonings, development plans and building permits

properties.name: Town of Nashville
properties.update_note: Adopted a 12-month moratorium 2026-08-04, missed by the snapshot.

properties.name: Town of Newport
properties.covers: permitting of data centers, data processing facilities, cryptocurrency mining and associated uses within the town and its extraterritorial jurisdiction
properties.update_note: Adopted a one-year moratorium 2026-09-10; the town's meeting notice fixes the date.

properties.name: Town of Weaverville
properties.covers: cryptocurrency mining and data centers reclassified as 'noxious uses', confined to industrial zones via conditional district review

properties.name: City of Hendersonville
properties.covers: acceptance, processing and approval of development approvals for data centers, cryptomining facilities, server farms and similar high-impact digital infrastructure facilities, including zoning, special use, site plan, building and conditional zoning approvals (per the draft ordinance)
properties.update_note: Reported adopted 2026-09-03 for 12 months; the city's packet has the ordinance, the vote is not in minutes yet.
properties.confirmation_note: The city's own agenda and packet confirm the September 3 hearing and the draft ordinance, but the vote itself is reported only by a specialist newsletter. Minutes are not posted; the council's next regular meeting is October 1.

properties.name: Town of Hildebran
properties.covers: development approvals for critical digital infrastructure facilities, the town's term for data centers and crypto mining
properties.update_note: Reported adopted 2026-08-24 for 12 months; the town's agenda confirms the hearing, the vote is not in minutes yet.
properties.confirmation_note: The town's own July 27 minutes and August 24 agenda confirm the council set out to adopt a twelve-month moratorium and held the hearing, but the vote is reported only by a specialist newsletter. August 24 minutes are not posted yet.

properties.name: Town of Whitakers
properties.update_note: Reported to have a moratorium in place; date and length not published.
properties.confirmation_note: The Rocky Mount Telegram states the town has a moratorium and a specialist newsletter dates it to June 2026, but no date, length, ordinance or minutes could be found; the town's website lists no 2026 minutes.
